_note: Chapter 1 script, first draft. Hotspot yaw/pitch values are rough guesses; place them for real with editor.html once the panoramas exist.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The front door of the Mistletoe Lounge. The doorbell was up where the tall people keep their secrets.

lines.speaker: granny
lines.text: Oh, for goodness' sake. I'll ring it. I'll wait out here, dear. Jazz gives me the drips.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Inside, the place was dark and warm and full of people pretending they weren't watching the door. Nobody watched me. Nobody ever does. It's my edge.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Up on stage, somebody new was singing in Jimmy's spotlight. The body wasn't even cold. Well. The body wasn't even a body.

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: Thank you, thank you. You're too kind. You're all too kind. Especially you in the front. Hello.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Cupid. Smooth as butter and just as alluring. Every eye in the room was on him. Every eye but mine. Mine were on his ankles. They were also very smooth.

lines.speaker: cupid
lines.text: This next one goes out to Jimmy Mittens. Rest easy, pal. And if you can hear me, you still owe me carrots.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A tribute and a debt in the same breath. That's show business. I filed it under suspicious, then under touching, then under suspicious again.

lines.speaker: vixen
lines.text: Well, well. A detective. And such a compact one.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Vixen. Lounge singer. She'd had this slot for years, until Jimmy took it. A dame with a motive and a beauty mark that moved around depending on the light.

lines.speaker: vixen
lines.text: You think I did it? Darling, I lost my slot to Jimmy, and tonight I lost it to Cupid. Clearly I'm not getting what I want.

lines.speaker: vixen
lines.text: If I were you, I'd ask the girl at the bar. The one whose hooves are on fire.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Pointing me at someone else. Classic. Only a guilty person would try to help me solve a crime.

lines.speaker: prancer
lines.text: Prancer. Jimmy's manager. Forty percent. Fifty on holidays. He was my boy, my client, my brand.

lines.speaker: easter_bunny
lines.text: And I'm just here networking. In December. At the North Pole. Totally normal.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The Easter Bunny. Out of season and out of his depth. I asked him where he was last night.

lines.speaker: easter_bunny
lines.text: I have an alibi. Here. This egg. It's hard-boiled.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A hard-boiled egg. I respected that. A fellow hard-boiled type. I let it slide.

lines.speaker: prancer
lines.text: Look, pal, if you want my professional opinion, Jimmy left with Comet. Tall, hot, steaming. You can't miss her.

lines.speaker: easter_bunny
lines.text: Comet. Definitely Comet. We'd both swear on the egg.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: They'd rehearsed it. Same name, same story. Somebody was coaching these two. I just didn't know who. Yet.

lines.speaker: dancer
lines.text: I choreographed Jimmy's act. Do you know what it's like teaching a snowman to move? He had no hips. He had a bottom ball.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Dancer. Hated the man's moves. Hated them enough to kill? I watched her closely. She did a little spin. I couldn't tell if it was a confession or a habit.

lines.speaker: dancer
lines.text: Listen. Last week, Comet tapped a little rhythm on this stage and set it on fire. Literally. We had to call the fire department.

lines.speaker: dancer
lines.text: Jimmy watched the whole thing and said, 'That's my kind of girl.'

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Three suspects. Three stories. All pointing in the same direction. You know what that tells me? It tells me they're covering for each other.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The question was who they were covering for. I needed a drink. Something cold. With a straw. A long straw.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Between me and the bar stood fourteen tables, a hat stand, and a reindeer doing the cha-cha. I plotted a route. Then I plotted a backup route. Then I walked in a straight line.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The bar. From down here, it was a polished wooden cliff with a brass foot rail I could use as a bench.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: At the far end, a lady reindeer with her hooves on fire was sipping something that had stopped being a drink and started being steam.

lines.speaker: silverbough
lines.text: Greetings, small traveler. I am Silverbough. I have tended this bar for four hundred winters. What shall it be?

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: An elf. One of the tall ones. Not the toy-making kind. The kind with flowing hair and a harp somewhere. We don't talk about each other at reunions.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A hot cocoa, Stretch. And whatever you know about Jimmy Mittens.

lines.speaker: silverbough
lines.text: In my homeland, we have no word for 'short.' We never needed one.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Cute. In mine, we have no word for 'quit.' We also have no word for 'ladder,' which is its own problem.

lines.speaker: silverbough
lines.text: Jimmy sat here last night, as he did every night. He was not alone. The stool beside him has not been the same since.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Through the tinsel goggles, the stool next to Jimmy's lit up like the Fourth of July. It was scorched black. Right through the cushion.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Somebody'd spilled a coffee here. A hot one. A very hot one. Possibly several hot coffees, over a period of years.

lines.speaker: silverbough
lines.text: That was not coffee.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I'll be the judge of what's coffee, Stretch.

lines.speaker: silverbough
lines.text: Allow me. Ascend, little one, as the eagle ascends.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: He set me on the bar like a drink order. I've been lifted by better. Not many.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A reserved card, standing on the bar where Jimmy sat. Table for two. It read: 'J. Mittens, plus C.'

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The C was scorched around the edges. Still warm.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: C. Could be anyone. Cupid. Carl. Carol. Some guy named Clive. A mysterious stranger simply known as 'the Letter C.'

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I ran through the alphabet twice. I kept coming back to C. Which, if you think about it, was very suspicious of C.

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Well, if it isn't my favorite little detective. Again.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Comet. The dame from the alley. Every suspect in this joint had said her name. That's how I knew she was the one person I could trust.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: Hold my drink, would you, sweetheart?

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Sure thing, sugar.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: She held it. It boiled. The glass whistled like a kettle and the ice cubes left the building. Must've been a warm room.

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Poor Jimmy. We sat right here last night. He said I made him feel like a new man. Then he said he felt a little light-headed. Then he said a lot of things. Then he was quiet.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: A grieving acquaintance. Sitting right where it happened. Some dames just can't let go.

lines.speaker: comet
lines.text: Well, I'd love to stay, sugar, but I've got practice at the training grounds. Laps. A girl's gotta stay warm.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: She swished out the door. The welcome mat caught fire. Nobody said anything. It's that kind of place.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: The training grounds. Where the whole Reindeer Squad goes to sweat. Every one of them with a motive, and every one of them pointing the same direction.

lines.speaker: tiny
lines.text: I knew what I had to do. I had to go to the training grounds and tail every reindeer in that squad. Except one. She'd been through enough.
